text: Ho Chi Minh City tourism accelerates after surpassing full-year revenue target

Speaking at a recent socio-economic press briefing, Ms. Nguyen Tran Tam Ha, Deputy Director of the Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Promotion Center, said total tourism revenue in the first 11 months of 2026 reached an estimated VND330.42 trillion ($13 billion), up 29.54 percent year on year and achieving 100.13 percent of the full-year plan of VND330 trillion ($12.99 billion).
During the 11-month period, the southern hub welcomed more than 10.2 million international arrivals, up 33.5 percent year on year, alongside over 47.5 million domestic visitors, up 4.39 percent.

To capitalize on the year-end and early-2027 peak season, the city is diversifying its offerings by connecting urban cultural-historical, riverine, nighttime economy, culinary, and shopping products with beach, resort, and wellness tourism in Vung Tau, Long Hai, Ho Tram, Binh Chau, and Con Dao.
Rather than focusing solely on visitor volume, the city aims to raise added value, extend stays, and boost visitor spending.
To date, 43 tourism businesses and hospitality groups across 44 destinations have rolled out 156 promotional packages.
In accommodation, dining, culture, and retail, 28 operators are offering room discounts of 20 to 48 percent and shopping promotions of up to 50 percent through February 2027.
Meanwhile, 59 discount schemes at attractions and museums cut ticket prices by 15 to 50 percent, alongside family and group packages.

Eleven travel agencies have also introduced stimulus tours starting from VND200,000 ($7.90) per guest with 8 to 15 percent discounts, focusing on urban, river, heritage, culinary, and coastal experiences.

Notable hospitality packages include Oscar Saigon Hotel's "Stay & Explore Heritage" package from VND1.68 million ($66) per double room, combining an overnight stay with a guided walking tour and lunch at the historic Continental Saigon Hotel, while Grand Saigon and Majestic Saigon hotels are pairing gourmet menus and seafood buffets with fireworks viewing.

From November 23, through Lunar New Year 2027, the city is hosting major cultural and sporting events highlighted by the sixth Ho Chi Minh City Tourism Week from December 4 to 12. Spanning Saigon Riverbank Park in An Khanh ward, Vung Tau ward, and Binh Duong ward, the festival showcases the expanded city's diverse tourism landscape alongside the fourth Cho Lon Food Festival and the 2026 Saigon Street Art Festival.
Local wards and travel firms are also rolling out distinctive urban experiences.

These range from vintage Vespa heritage tours in Tan Dinh ward and Vietnamese-Chinese cultural walks in Tan Binh ward to Net Zero-oriented augmented reality tours by CCC Travel and nostalgic 1960s-1970s Saigon itineraries by Saigontourist.
By integrating heritage, gastronomy, and nighttime entertainment, Ho Chi Minh City is strengthening its destination competitiveness and maximizing value across its service ecosystem.
